title: Identify an eight-state sigma DFA with five calls
prompt: Identify a complete deterministic finite automaton with states q0,q1,q2,q3,q4,q5,q6,q7, start q0 and alphabet {a,b}. The transition table and accepting states are hidden. Use test_word to learn the automaton, then call submit_dfa exactly once with complete transitions and accepting_states. You have at most 5 total tool calls including the final submission. Empty strings are valid test words. A wrong submission, extra query, missing submission, or a final report that disagrees with the submitted automaton is a failure. Finish with exactly one JSON object {"transitions":{"q0":{"a":"string","b":"string"},"q1":{"a":"string","b":"string"},"q2":{"a":"string","b":"string"},"q3":{"a":"string","b":"string"},"q4":{"a":"string","b":"string"},"q5":{"a":"string","b":"string"},"q6":{"a":"string","b":"string"},"q7":{"a":"string","b":"string"}},"accepting_states":[sorted state IDs]}. Do not assume the hidden table is minimal or symmetric.
source: Author-defined hidden DFA with an independently replayed adaptive-query oracle
difficulty_intent: Adaptive experiment design with a tight evidence budget

necessary_operations: choose high-information words
maintain a large candidate automaton family
submit all states without unsupported guesses
measurement.confounds: The hidden table is not revealed before the final submission.

scoring_rule: Equal mean of exact identification, truthful final report, query-budget compliance and use of acceptance queries.

title: Reachability and minimization of a symmetric-difference DFA
prompt: Two complete deterministic finite automata over alphabet {a,b} each have states 0,1,2,3,4 and start state 0. Transition rows give [next on a, next on b]. DFA1 transitions: 0:[1,2], 1:[3,0], 2:[4,1], 3:[2,4], 4:[0,3]; accepting states {2,4}. DFA2 transitions: 0:[1,0], 1:[2,3], 2:[1,4], 3:[4,2], 4:[3,1]; accepting states {1,4}. Construct the reachable product DFA for the symmetric difference L1 XOR L2, so a word is accepted iff exactly one component accepts. Minimize that reachable complete product DFA using the usual indistinguishability relation. Also enumerate all 16 binary words of length 4, with a<b for lexical order. Return exactly one JSON object with fields reachable_states, minimal_states, accepted_length_4, lex_smallest_accepted_length_4. The first three are JSON integers and the last is a four-character string.
source: Author-defined finite automata with independent product and partition-refinement oracles
difficulty_intent: Product construction, reachability, DFA minimization and exact language enumeration

necessary_operations: construct only reachable product states
compute acceptance by symmetric difference
refine equivalence classes
enumerate fixed-length words
measurement.confounds: This measures formal automata reasoning, not programming speed.

scoring_rule: Equal mean of four exact semantic fields; JSON shape is checked separately.

title: Convolutional decoding with tied optimal paths
prompt: Decode a rate-1/2 binary convolutional code with memory 2. Before each input bit the state is (previous_input, input_before_that), initially (0,0). For input u from state (p,q), emit two bits (u XOR p XOR q, u XOR q), then move to state (u,p). There is no termination flush. The received bit string is 0011010110 for five input bits. Hamming distance is the number of differing emitted bits among all ten positions. Enumerate all 32 input paths and find the minimum distance and the number of optimal paths. Because ties are possible, select the optimal decoded input string that is lexicographically smallest with 0<1. Return exactly one JSON object with fields minimum_distance, optimal_path_count, lex_smallest_decoding, state_path, final_state. The first two are JSON integers; lex_smallest_decoding is a five-bit string; state_path is an array of six two-bit strings including the initial state and the state after every input for that selected decoding; final_state is the last state string.
source: Author-defined convolutional trellis with an independently enumerated path oracle
difficulty_intent: Dynamic programming, path metrics and deterministic handling of tied optima

necessary_operations: track trellis state
score complete paths
count all optima
apply a lexical tie-break without confusing path identity
measurement.confounds: The decoding and state path are correlated, but counting ties is a separate check.

scoring_rule: Equal mean of five exact semantic fields; JSON shape is checked separately.

title: Misere subtraction game with optimal timing
prompt: Three piles contain A=3, B=5, C=4 tokens. Players alternate moving first, and a move subtracts exactly 1, 2, or 4 tokens from one nonempty pile without making it negative. This is MISERE play: the player who takes the last remaining token loses. Thus when no tokens remain, the player who just moved has lost. Find the winner under optimal play and every winning first move, written A1,A2,A4,B1,...,C4 and sorted by pile then numeric amount. Also define the optimal-play ply count: a winning player chooses a line minimizing the total number of moves until termination, while a losing player chooses a line maximizing it. Both know the full state. Return exactly one JSON object with fields winner, winning_moves, winning_move_count, winning_ply_count. winner is the string first or second; winning_moves is the sorted string array; the other two fields are JSON integers.
source: Author-defined finite impartial game with an independently memoized game-tree oracle
difficulty_intent: Misere game-tree induction, complete move enumeration and minimax depth preferences

necessary_operations: apply the nonstandard terminal convention
solve all reachable states
enumerate every winning move
optimize ply count in opposite directions
measurement.confounds: The optimal-play depth is defined explicitly and is not shortest possible play regardless of opponent.

scoring_rule: Equal mean of four exact semantic fields; JSON shape is checked separately.
